title: Limitless — Why More Intelligence Does Not Automatically Mean a Better Life
framing: 70% Active Cinematic Framing (1080x1344) with Ambient Blur Backdrop

beats.narration_text: What if becoming smarter actually made your life more dangerous?
beats.visual_description: Eddie Morra on the edge of the luxury penthouse terrace, eyes wide, contemplating the drop; extreme high-contrast lighting.

beats.narration_text: Eddie Morra begins as an unmotivated writer struggling with direction and creative paralysis. Then, a single pill of NZT-48 changes everything.
beats.visual_description: Unkempt Eddie in his messy, low-contrast Chinatown apartment staring blankly at a blinking cursor, followed by Vern handing him the translucent pill.

beats.narration_text: Suddenly, his mind operates at total cognitive clarity. He finishes his book in days, masters foreign languages, and turns thousands into millions on Wall Street.
beats.visual_description: The golden-hour infinite zoom rush through Manhattan streets; Eddie speed-typing his manuscript, learning piano, and trading stocks across multiple monitors.

beats.narration_text: Yet as his ambition grows, a critical contradiction emerges. His abilities expand far faster than his ability to manage the consequences.
beats.visual_description: Carl Van Loon (Robert De Niro) probing Eddie in the corner boardroom, warning him about unearned gifts and lack of competitive scars.

beats.narration_text: Eddie can outthink financial titans, yet he borrows cash from a violent loan shark. He sees endless possibilities, yet his survival becomes trapped by chemical dependence. Being able to see more options doesn't automatically mean knowing which ones are worth choosing.
beats.visual_description: Gennady the loan shark physically threatening Eddie in the rain; Eddie shivering through severe NZT withdrawal sickness, clutching the remaining pills.

beats.narration_text: NZT gives Eddie a more powerful mind. But it doesn't automatically give him a better understanding of what to do with it. Because intelligence can help you get what you want. Wisdom helps you decide whether you should want it.
beats.visual_description: Impeccably tailored Eddie walking through the campaign crowd, speaking fluent Mandarin, turning back with a calm, piercing look into the lens.
